questions.prompt: Which type of tooth is shaped for cutting food?
questions.explanation: Incisors have thin edges that bite and cut food.

questions.prompt: Why does a bicycle slow when the rider stops pedalling?

options.text: Gravity stops acting on the bicycle whenever pedalling stops
Friction and air resistance oppose its motion
The wheels lose all their mass

questions.explanation: Friction at moving parts and tyres, together with air resistance, removes motion energy.

questions.prompt: Which change is readily reversible?
questions.explanation: Ice can melt back into liquid water without forming a new substance.

questions.prompt: What are ordinary clouds mainly made from?

options.text: Only invisible water vapour with no liquid droplets at all
Tiny water droplets or ice crystals

questions.explanation: Cooling water vapour forms tiny droplets or ice crystals that can be seen as clouds.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a switch in a simple circuit?

options.text: To open or close the electrical path
To create electrical energy from nothing
To measure the mass of the cell

questions.explanation: A switch controls current by completing or breaking the conducting path.

questions.prompt: How can camouflage help a small animal survive?

options.text: It supplies the animal with food
It makes the animal harder to see
It changes the animal into a plant

questions.explanation: Blending with the surroundings can help an animal avoid predators or approach prey.

questions.prompt: Which tool best separates gravel from dry sand?
questions.explanation: A sieve lets smaller sand grains pass while retaining larger gravel pieces.

questions.prompt: Which instrument is most suitable for measuring 35 mL of water?
questions.explanation: A graduated measuring cylinder is designed to measure liquid volume.

questions.prompt: Why can you see your face in a smooth mirror?

options.text: Light reflects regularly from its surface
The mirror produces a copy of your face
Sound waves carry the image to your eyes
The glass absorbs every ray of light

questions.explanation: A smooth mirror reflects light in an orderly way so an image reaches your eyes.

questions.prompt: A balloon expands when air is blown into it. What does this show?
questions.explanation: The added air takes up volume and pushes the balloon's surface outwards.

questions.prompt: Why are seasons opposite in Australia and much of Europe?

options.text: Earth moves much closer to the Sun during each Australian summer
The Moon cools one continent at a time
Their hemispheres tilt towards the Sun at different times

questions.explanation: Earth's tilted axis makes the two hemispheres receive more direct sunlight at opposite times.

questions.prompt: Which organism is a consumer?
questions.explanation: A wallaby obtains energy by eating other organisms, so it is a consumer.

questions.prompt: Which tool should time how long a toy car rolls?
questions.explanation: A stopwatch measures elapsed time.

questions.prompt: A sealed empty plastic bottle floats, but the same bottle filled with sand sinks. What best explains this?

options.text: Sand removes gravity from the bottle
Filling it increases its average density
The water becomes less dense nearby
The bottle's plastic changes into metal

questions.explanation: Adding sand increases mass greatly without a similar volume increase, so average density rises.

questions.prompt: A student's pulse is counted before and after running. Why does it usually increase after running?

options.text: The heart stops sending oxygen-rich blood to every working muscle
Lungs no longer take in oxygen
Muscles need oxygen and nutrients delivered faster

questions.explanation: Working muscles need faster delivery and waste removal, so the heart pumps more often.

questions.prompt: Why is rusting classed as a chemical change?

options.text: The iron is cut into smaller pieces
A new substance forms on the iron

questions.explanation: Rust has different properties from iron and forms through a reaction with oxygen and water.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Recognise formation of a new substance

questions.prompt: Two globes are on separate branches of a parallel circuit. One globe breaks. What is most likely?

options.text: The other branch can remain lit
Current flows only through the broken globe

questions.explanation: Separate branches provide another complete path when one branch fails.

questions.prompt: A hillside with plants loses less soil during rain than bare soil. Why?

options.text: Plants increase the speed of run-off down the entire hillside
Roots hold soil and leaves reduce raindrop impact
Roots turn soil into solid rock

questions.explanation: Vegetation anchors particles and softens the impact of falling water.

questions.prompt: A graph of plant growth has time on the horizontal axis. What should normally be on the vertical axis?

options.text: The date the question was written

questions.explanation: The vertical axis shows the dependent measurement, such as height or leaf count.

questions.prompt: Four cups are wrapped in different materials and filled with equally hot water. Which evidence best identifies the best insulator?

options.text: The cup with the brightest wrapping
The cup measured with the largest thermometer
The cup closest to the classroom door
The cup with the smallest temperature decrease

questions.explanation: The best insulation slows energy transfer, producing the smallest cooling change under equal conditions.

questions.prompt: A habitat provides organisms with resources such as food, water and shelter.
questions.explanation: A habitat is the place that supplies conditions and resources an organism needs.

questions.prompt: A moving object can change direction even if its speed stays the same.
questions.explanation: A force can turn an object while its speed remains constant.

questions.prompt: Melting wax always creates a completely new substance.
questions.explanation: Melting changes state; the wax can solidify again as the same substance.

questions.prompt: Groundwater can collect in spaces and cracks within soil and rock.
questions.explanation: Water infiltrates and may be stored in permeable underground materials.

questions.prompt: A fair comparison can use different measuring tools for each test group without consequence.
questions.explanation: Using the same suitable tool reduces measurement differences between groups.

questions.prompt: All offspring of the same parents are genetically identical.
questions.explanation: Sexual reproduction combines inherited information differently, producing variation.

questions.prompt: Increasing the length of a shadow proves the light source became brighter.
questions.explanation: Shadow length mainly depends on the relative positions of source, object and surface, not brightness alone.

questions.prompt: A conclusion should describe what the evidence supports, even when it differs from the prediction.
questions.explanation: Scientific conclusions follow results rather than being changed to preserve a prediction.

questions.prompt: Which TWO structures protect important organs in the human body?
questions.explanation: The skull protects the brain and the rib cage surrounds the heart and lungs.

questions.prompt: Which TWO changes would make a toy car travel farther after leaving a ramp?

options.text: Add a brake that rubs the wheel

questions.explanation: Lower axle friction and a smoother path reduce forces that slow the car.

questions.prompt: Which TWO observations suggest a new substance formed?

options.text: Water is poured into another cup

questions.explanation: Gas production and formation of a new precipitate are evidence of chemical change.

questions.prompt: Which TWO factors can change how quickly water infiltrates soil?
questions.explanation: Particle spaces and compaction control how easily water can move through soil.

questions.prompt: Which TWO steps reduce bias when testing people's preferred fruit?
questions.explanation: A varied sample and neutral wording make the results more representative and less leading.

questions.prompt: Which TWO statements are supported when a metal spoon warms faster than a wooden spoon in hot water?

options.text: The metal transfers thermal energy faster
The wood is a better insulator

questions.explanation: The observation supports better conduction by metal and better insulation by wood.

questions.prompt: Which TWO consequences could follow a sharp decline in insect pollinators?

options.text: Animals relying on those fruits lose food

questions.explanation: Reduced pollination can lower seed and fruit production, affecting animals that feed on them.

questions.prompt: Which TWO features make a scientific explanation stronger?

options.text: It states that no other explanation is possible
It connects evidence to a scientific idea
It ignores results that do not fit

questions.explanation: A strong explanation links relevant observations to scientific concepts and acknowledges evidence honestly.

questions.prompt: Order the pathway of food through these digestive organs.
questions.explanation: Food is chewed in the mouth, passes to the stomach, then through the small intestine and large intestine.

questions.prompt: Order the events when a book slides to rest on a table.
questions.explanation: The push starts motion; friction opposes it, speed decreases, and the book stops.

items.text: A push gives the book motion

questions.prompt: Order the steps for comparing how quickly three materials absorb water.
questions.explanation: Equal samples receive equal water and time, their absorption is measured, then results are compared.

items.text: Add equal water volumes for equal times
Measure the water each sample absorbs

questions.prompt: Order these events in the formation of rain from surface water.
questions.explanation: Surface water evaporates, vapour rises and cools, droplets form, and sufficiently large droplets fall.

items.text: Droplets become heavy enough to fall
